Quasi-closed orbit of the captured pairs (44 of 50 bound events):
  T  minimum 0.056043 fs
  T  mean    213.032 fs
  T  maximum 4801.06 fs
  revolutions observed: minimum 4.16575e-05, mean 0.164226, maximum 3.56869
T is the Kepler period of the osculating capture orbit, the longer of its capture-time and window-close values.
The revolution count is what the bound observation window actually covered, NOT a count to collapse: these pairs are
followed only long enough to classify them, so the window is bounded by boundObservationTimeCap.

Bound-state CREM collapse time (1 of 50 bound events):
  minimum 5.67018e-06 ps
  mean    5.67018e-06 ps
  maximum 5.67018e-06 ps
This is the extrapolated classical inspiral time to the pair's inner boundary (the Compton barrier for e+e-,
the collision boundary for every other pair) from the orbit-averaged radiated power (secular
dE/dt=P model; experiments 1 and 2 now measure this mechanically instead, so the two are NOT comparable).  It is not a quantum
annihilation lifetime.  Only bound events whose observation window closed a full Kepler orbit are included:
below that the window samples the post-periapsis leg, whose instantaneous power is not an orbit average.
  43 of 50 bound events were excluded by that gate (window shorter than one orbit).
